answer: The kernel counter is kept in dune and onyx makes public each reset. Anyone as a result has to keep each extra identity continuously active for 44 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. A bond is refunded only after 44 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. Each duplicate costs another 185 dollars in locked collateral and another 4 days of waiting. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
